table2_ablation_comparison.description: Primary comparison at item budgets 10, 50, 100 and 500. Each scored row submitted_<budget> is the submitted method run by the evaluator through the item-query protocol on every checkpoint of the slice's LMs and all six benchmarks, with at most <budget> items per checkpoint-benchmark session. RANDOM and RANDOM IRT are computed by the evaluator itself (five fixed random subsets) and reported unranked under 'baselines'. Paper values below are the paper's Table 2 (FLUID BENCHMARKING in the submitted rows), averaged over all six LMs; each gym slice holds three LMs.

rank_distance.description: Mean absolute OLL-reference rank deviation between paired benchmarks. Measures cross-benchmark validity: good selection should rank LM checkpoints consistently across related benchmarks.

total_variation.description: Normalized total variation of score curves across checkpoints. Measures score stability: good selection should produce smooth, non-oscillating score progressions.

saturation.description: Absolute Spearman rank correlation between checkpoint index and score level. Measures learning curve shape: good selection should show monotonic improvement rather than flat or noisy curves.

appendix_h_full_accuracy_comparison.description: Appendix H: the submitted method at 500 items against full-benchmark accuracy (all items, computed by the evaluator and reported unranked under 'baselines', together with all-item MAP ability). The scored row is the submitted method's 500-item result. Paper values: Appendix H over all six LMs.

rank_distance.description: Mean absolute OLL-reference rank deviation between paired benchmarks. Measures cross-benchmark validity.

total_variation.description: Normalized total variation of score curves. Measures score stability.

saturation.description: Absolute Spearman rank correlation of checkpoint index vs score level. Measures learning curve shape.

appendix_f_table4_worst_lm_100.description: Per-LM consistency (Appendix F, Table 4) at 100 items, scored as the worst LM of the slice: the largest per-LM rank distance, the largest per-LM total variation and the smallest per-LM saturation of the submitted method. A method that is good on average but fails on one training trajectory scores badly here. Per-LM values of the submitted method and of the evaluator's baselines are reported unranked under 'per_lm'.

rank_distance.description: Largest per-LM mean OLL-reference rank distance between paired benchmarks (validity) across the slice LMs.

total_variation.description: Largest per-LM mean normalized total variation of checkpoint score curves (variance) across the slice LMs.

saturation.description: Smallest per-LM mean absolute Spearman monotonicity of checkpoint score curves (saturation) across the slice LMs.

appendix_f_table4_worst_lm_100._note: results are the worst-LM values derived from the paper's Table 4 over all six LMs (rank distance and TV: maximum over LMs; saturation: minimum). The gym's train and test slices hold three LMs each, so a slice's worst LM is not on exactly the paper's scale.

_notes.setup: Released IRT parameters and item-level checkpoint responses (Hugging Face allenai/fluid-benchmarking, revision e0a11a3). Responses are binarized at 0.5 like the paper's released loader. The released K2 table has 46 checkpoints (paper: 61): 452 checkpoints / 2,712 checkpoint-benchmark pairs instead of 467 / 2,802.
_notes.slices: train = Amber-6.7B, OLMo1-7B, OLMo2-7B (visible); test = K2-65B, Pythia-2.8B, Pythia-6.9B (hidden).
_notes.paper_values: All 'results' values are the paper's reported numbers (Tables 2 and 4, Appendix H), unchanged; only the proposed-method rows were renamed from fluid_* to submitted_*.
